title: Marguerite and the Will
premise: Vesper Okafor, a concierge at the Hotel Aurelia who has built a career on noticing what guests hide, receives two letters from Marguerite Delacroix-Ashford: one confessing to a death thirty years ago, one promising Vesper an inheritance if she attends the family's anniversary dinner. Drawn into the Delacroix estate under the guise of event staff, Vesper discovers the confession describes the drowning of Marguerite's first husband—a man whose alibi was quietly manufactured by three people still seated at the table. As the anniversary approaches, each guest tries to recruit or silence her, and Vesper realizes the inheritance is bait: Marguerite wants a witness who owes her nothing. At the dinner, Vesper exposes the truth not as accusation but as testimony, forcing the family to choose between their name and their souls; Marguerite dies peacefully days later, leaving Vesper not money but the letters themselves—and the choice of what to do with them.
about_author: Elodie Delacroix is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk who spent a decade listening to other people's secrets in hotel lobbies across the French Riviera and coastal New England. They write mysteries about people whose jobs require them to be invisible.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes
chapters.summary: Vesper Okafor, concierge at the Hotel Aurelia, opens two letters from a dying stranger: a confession to murder and a promise of inheritance. Her POV establishes her rule—never take a case she can't close—and the tremor of fear that this one may close her instead. Beat: curiosity overriding caution.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Watched Lobbies
chapters.summary: Vesper researches Marguerite Delacroix-Ashford through old guest ledgers and newspaper archives, learning of the first husband, Edmund, drowned in 1994, ruled accidental. Flashback-tinged third person reveals why Vesper became someone who notices everything. Beat: the past has teeth.

chapters.title: Invitation to the Estate
chapters.summary: A second letter arrives with a contract: attend the anniversary dinner as hired event staff, observe, report back. Vesper accepts against her own instincts. Her POV captures the humiliation and thrill of crossing from servant to investigator. Beat: signing away neutrality.

chapters.title: Ashcombe House
chapters.summary: Vesper arrives at the crumbling Delacroix estate and maps its geography—the boathouse, the drained pool, portraits with eyes scratched out. The housekeeper, Ruth, recognizes something in Vesper's face and warns her off. Beat: unease dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: Three Alibis
chapters.summary: Vesper identifies the anniversary guests who were present in 1994: brother-in-law Julian, business partner Sefu, and Marguerite's sister Colette. Each has a polished story about the night Edmund drowned. Her POV catalogs contradictions like a concierge cataloging lies. Beat: the pattern begins.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Preparations for the thirtieth-anniversary dinner expose family fault lines; Vesper overhears Julian bribing the caterer and Colette burning correspondence. Someone searches Vesper's quarters. Beat: she is no longer invisible, and it terrifies her.

chapters.title: What Ruth Remembers
chapters.summary: Ruth, the housekeeper who was a maid in 1994, tells Vesper about the storm that night and the boat found rowed back to shore empty. Her POV shifts to Ruth's trembling testimony. Beat: grief older than the crime.

chapters.title: The Confession Reread
chapters.summary: Vesper rereads Marguerite's confession and finds a deliberate gap: Marguerite admits presence but not act. She realizes the letter is a test—or a trap meant for someone else entirely. Beat: the ground tilts.

chapters.title: Julian's Offer
chapters.summary: Julian corners Vesper with money and menace, revealing he knows who she is. He offers triple the inheritance to confirm Marguerite is senile. Vesper's POV wrestles with contempt and temptation. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Sefu's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vesper discovers Sefu kept accounts from 1994—payments routed through the hotel where she works, implicating her own mentor, the late head concierge Marcel. Beat: the case reaches into her own history.

chapters.title: Colette's Version
chapters.summary: Colette, drunk on sherry, gives a third account: Edmund was violent, Marguerite protected herself, and the alibi was mercy, not conspiracy. Vesper can no longer tell which version is survival and which is sin. Beat: sympathy complicating judgment.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Vesper searches the boathouse at night and finds Edmund's watch, kept thirty years, engraved with a date that isn't his wedding anniversary. Someone follows her; she escapes by routes only hotel staff know. Beat: hunted in open country.

chapters.title: Marguerite, Alive
chapters.summary: Finally granted an audience, Vesper meets Marguerite—sharp, dying, unrepentant and terrified in equal measure. Marguerite admits she wrote the confession to force the truth into the open before she dies, but refuses to say what actually happened. Beat: love against duty, stated plainly.

chapters.title: Marcel's File
chapters.summary: Vesper returns to the Aurelia and opens Marcel's locked drawer: he manufactured the 1994 alibis for pay, and left her a note naming the true witness. Her POV grieves the man who taught her to notice. Beat: betrayal by the dead.

chapters.title: The True Witness
chapters.summary: The note leads to a retired police diver living quietly upcoast, who confirms the drowning was staged—but says the person he saw on the water that night was not Marguerite. Beat: every certainty inverted.

chapters.title: Countdown Dinner
chapters.summary: Two days before the anniversary, threats escalate: Ruth is dismissed, Vesper's room is searched again, and a fire nearly takes the west wing archives. She realizes someone wants the past ash before the toast. Beat: rising dread.

chapters.title: The Salvaged Letters
chapters.summary: From the smoke-damaged archive Vesper recovers Edmund's own letters—he had discovered the family's fraud and planned to leave, taking the evidence. The motive reframes: not passion, but protection of an empire. Beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Vesper lays out the whole architecture—alibis, payments, the watch, the diver's account—and finds the shape of it: three people covered for one, and only one of them knew why. She drafts her testimony and hesitates over the final name. Beat: the weight of knowing.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: At the raised glasses, Vesper speaks—not as accuser but as witness, laying the truth on the tablecloth like a place setting. The guilty one breaks; the others must choose between silence and each other. Climax: the toast becomes a trial.

chapters.title: Confession, Corrected
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, the true actor confesses privately to Vesper and to Marguerite: it was done to protect Marguerite, without her knowledge—her guilt was borrowed, worn for thirty years. Beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Marguerite dies at dawn. The will leaves the family money and Vesper only the two letters and a line: 'For the one who noticed.' The family scatters; Ruth stays; the house will become something new. Beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Concierge, No Longer Invisible
chapters.summary: Vesper returns to the Aurelia, places the letters in her safe, and chooses to keep them—neither weapon nor trophy, but memory. She takes a new guest's coat and notices, once more, everything. Final beat: survival paid for, and worth it.
